analysis.investment_thesis: Methodhub shows explosive revenue growth (35→135 Cr in 2Y) and headline ROE of 42.7%, but promoter holding of just 26.85%, a debt-laden balance sheet unusual for IT services, and poor cash conversion (OCF 5 Cr vs PAT 11 Cr) make this a speculative micro-cap rather than a conviction bet. I want clean cash flows and real promoter skin-in-the-game — this has neither.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR ~96% (35→135 Cr) with PAT up 11x in 2 years
Headline ROE 42.7% and ROCE 31.1% are top-decile
Valuation reasonable at 14x P/E in a structurally growing IT sector
key_risks: Promoter holding only 26.85% — well below my 50%+ India threshold
Borrowings 39 Cr vs equity 57 Cr is anomalous for an IT services firm
OCF (5 Cr) vs PAT (11 Cr) shows weak cash conversion — earnings quality suspect
red_flags: Low promoter holding (26.85%) in a recently-listed micro-cap
Equity jumped from 11 to 57 Cr in one year — major dilution/fresh issue
IT services business carrying high debt with finance cost eating ~30% of EBITDA
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The top-line story is dazzling — revenue more than doubled from 57 to 135 Cr in FY25, EBITDA margin holds at ~13%, and headline ROE of 42.7% looks world-class. At 14x earnings with a 144 Cr market cap, this fits the "small-to-midcap transition" archetype I hunt for. But in Indian micro-cap IT, the numbers must be stress-tested. Promoter holding of only 26.85% is a fundamental dealbreaker — in India, promoter skin-in-the-game is how you sleep at night, and below 50% you're essentially betting on professional management of a company with no track record.

The balance sheet deepens my skepticism. An IT services firm with 39 Cr of borrowings (D/E ~0.68) is anomalous — software consulting shouldn't need that kind of leverage unless receivables are bloated or there's inorganic activity. The 4x jump in equity base (11→57 Cr) signals a recent capital raise that also diluted the promoter. Most telling: OCF of 5 Cr against PAT of 11 Cr means earnings aren't translating into cash — classic warning sign in Indian small-cap IT. I'd rather pay 25x for Persistent or LTIMindtree than 14x for an unproven micro-cap with governance question marks. Avoid until promoter stake rises, debt falls, and cash conversion normalizes over 2-3 years.
